card: Makes addrman address selection inside buckets uniformly random across occupied slots. Previously, selecting from a bucket used a linear scan from a random offset, which heavily biased peer selection toward addresses following large runs of empty slots (up to 95.3% vs 4.7% in a two-address bucket). The PR copies occupied bucket entries into a buffer and samples uniformly with network filtering, and adds unit and fuzz tests.
changed_since_previous: Now includes concrete implementation, a unit test checking uniform distribution and network filtering, and an assertion in the addrman fuzz target.
evidence: PR description: 'if for example only position 17 and 20 contain an address, 17 will be picked with probability 95.3% (whenever the initial position is 21..63 or 0..17) and 20 will be picked with probability 4.7%'
PR description: 'Suggested by Crypt-iQ. Also pointed out earlier by mzumsande in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/23140#discussion_r733084509.'
problem: When selecting an address from an addrman bucket, nodes pick a random position in the 64-slot bucket and scan forward until hitting an occupied entry. Sparse buckets heavily bias selection toward entries preceded by empty slots (for instance, an entry following 61 empty slots has a 95.3% selection chance while another entry has 4.7%), skewing outbound connection selection.

risk.why: A bug in addrman address selection could cause infinite loops or fail to return valid peer addresses for outbound connections.

summary: Makes address selection within addrman buckets uniformly random across occupied slots. Instead of linearly scanning from a random offset until an occupied slot is found, non-empty entries are collected into a temporary buffer and sampled uniformly while applying network filtering.
